images.title: Eights sit on fours
images.purpose: Show that every multiple of 8 is also a multiple of 4, so nobody says just vada.
images.composition: Two dot rows stacked on a shared number line, the lower row is the multiples of 4 and the upper row is the multiples of 8, with wide white space.
images.exact_structure: One grey #6B7280 horizontal line from 0 to 32. Lower row: exactly 8 amber #E69F00 dots at 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32. Upper row: exactly 4 larger teal #0072B2 dots at 8, 16, 24, 32, each directly above an amber dot, joined by a thin grey vertical line. Exactly 2 rows, 12 dots.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a teal dot not directly above an amber dot
images.takeaway: Every multiple of 8 is also a multiple of 4.
images.description: A line from 0 to 32 with 8 amber dots for multiples of 4 and 4 teal dots for multiples of 8 directly above four of them.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at each teal dot and say which amber dot is under it.

image_decisions.why: One clean picture carries the main idea of this concept.
